title: NodeKit observation pack
description:
LEARN stage of the Builder Journey. Answers: what actually happened after launch, FROM WHICH SOURCE, and what did NOT get observed. Consumes LaunchManifest + StoryPack; closes the loop back to DECIDE.

The defining problem of this stage is that absence of observation is the NORMAL case and must never read as a negative finding. 'no errors observed' and 'error observation was never instrumented' are different claims, so they live in structurally different places: the first is a `coverage.observed` report with outcome `no-instances` and a non-zero sampleCount; the second is a `coverage.unobserved` report that CANNOT carry a sampleCount, an outcome or a conclusion at all. There is no shape in which the two can be confused.

Coverage is a partition, not a list. Every dimension in the closed enum appears exactly once, in exactly one of `observed` / `unobserved` — enforced by the allOf at the bottom of this file. A stage cannot narrow its own scope by omitting a dimension, which is the vacuous pass this schema exists to prevent (docs/VACUOUS_PASS.md).

Does NOT define a friction record. `content.observations[]` is deliberately field-identical to the friction records `src/lib/friction-loop.mjs#collectFriction` already reads (id, severity, kind, observed, consequence), so classification into the existing loop is an identity map, not a translation. Judging is owned by nodekit.builder-gym-verdict/v1, recorded human friction by nodekit.human-study-event/v1, and the decision record by nodekit.evolution-event/v1. This pack feeds all three and replaces none.

caseId.description: Identical across all five journey artifacts for one journey.

inputs.description: Binding, not a label. sha256 is over the canonical JSON (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace) of the upstream artifact. LEARN consumes LaunchManifest and StoryPack, so both digests must be present; a pack that cannot digest what it consumed was handed a name, not an artifact.

allOf.description: The LaunchManifest this pack observed the consequences of.
The StoryPack whose claims this pack checks against reality.

completeness.description: An empty notRun is itself a claim: that everything in scope was attempted. A refusal with a reason is a success; a silent omission is the failure this apparatus exists to catch.

instant.description: ISO-8601 UTC, Z-terminated. A local-offset timestamp makes two observation windows incomparable.

window.description: A closed interval. Every measurement states its own window, because a finding without a window is not comparable to the next run's finding.

dimension.description:
CLOSED on purpose. An open dimension set lets a pack narrow its own scope by simply never mentioning a dimension, which is exactly the omission this stage must make impossible. Adding a dimension is a schema version bump, not a producer's private choice.

reachability: is the launched thing actually reachable. usage: did anyone use it. errors: runtime failures. performance: latency and responsiveness. taskOutcome: did users complete the primary job from the OpportunityContract. friction: where users struggled. cost: spend against the standing grant declared in the LaunchManifest. feedback: direct human statements about it.

source.description: WHERE an observation could come from. A source that exists is not a source that reports; `availability` keeps those apart.

locator.description: Where the source physically is: a URL, a repository-relative path, a provider dashboard identifier. A source nobody can go and re-read is an assertion.

availability.description: not-configured and configured-not-reporting are the two states that most often masquerade as a clean result. Neither may ever back an `observed` report.

instrument.description: HOW a source was read. `measures` and `method` are required because docs/VACUOUS_PASS.md's rule is that an instrument must state what it measured, not only what it concluded. An instrument that cannot name its quantity and its unit did not measure anything.

sourceId.description: Must match a content.sources[].sourceId. Referential integrity is a verifier's job, not JSON Schema's.

measures.description: The quantity, WITH its unit. 'count of HTTP 5xx responses per hour', not 'errors'.

method.description: How the quantity was obtained, precisely enough for a second party to obtain it again.

status.description: not-implemented means the instrument is described here but does not exist. Describing an instrument is not running one; only `ran` may back an `observed` report.

observedReport.description: A dimension that was actually watched. Requires the source and the instrument that watched it, so a reader can tell what the number is a number OF.

measured.description: What was measured and what came back, in units. Stated separately from `conclusion` so a conclusion can be checked against its own evidence.

sampleCount.description: How many units of observation the instrument actually saw (requests, sessions, probe runs, reports). This is the number that separates 'we watched and there were none' from 'we watched nothing'.

outcome.description: no-instances is the ONLY way to say 'none observed', and it is a positive claim requiring sampleCount >= 1. Zero samples is `inconclusive` — the instrument ran but the world did not supply anything to measure, which supports no statement about the dimension at all.

findings.description: References into content.observations[].id. Non-empty only when outcome is `findings`.

conclusion.description: Optional, and never a substitute for `measured`.

allOf.description: 'No errors observed' from zero samples is the flagship vacuous pass. A no-instances claim must be backed by at least one thing actually looked at.

unobservedReport.description: A dimension that was NOT watched. This is a first-class report with its own required fields, not an omission and not a result. It structurally cannot carry sampleCount, outcome, findings or conclusion, so it can never be misread as a negative finding.

state.description: not-instrumented: nothing exists that could have seen this. instrumented-not-run: an instrument exists and was not executed. source-unavailable: the instrument ran but its source could not be read. outside-window: the dimension is only observable outside this pack's window. refused: deliberately not observed, on authority or privacy grounds.

reason.description: Why it was not observed. A reason is what turns a gap into a finding about the instrumentation.

wouldRequire.description: The specific instrument or access that WOULD observe this dimension. This is the field that closes the loop: an unobserved dimension is an input to the next DECIDE, not a dead end.

sourceIds.description: The sources that were expected to serve this dimension, when any existed.

instrumentIds.description: Instruments declared for this dimension that did not produce a reading.

blocksClaims.description: Claims from the bound StoryPack that cannot be substantiated because of this gap. An unobserved dimension with no blocked claims is a gap nobody was relying on; one with blocked claims is a hole under a promise already made to a human.

observation.description:
One recorded post-launch fact.

The first five fields are field-identical to the friction records `src/lib/friction-loop.mjs#collectFriction` already normalises out of harness/journey/*.json (id, severity, kind, observed, consequence). Classifying this pack into the existing loop is therefore `{ friction: pack.content.observations }` — an identity map. This schema deliberately does NOT introduce a competing friction record type; nodekit.human-study-* owns recorded human friction and test/repo-tour.test.mjs enforces that ownership.

The remaining fields are the provenance the friction record never carried: which source, which instrument, and whether the fact was measured or inferred.

severity.description: Same ladder as src/lib/friction-loop.mjs SEVERITY_ORDER, so ordering survives the handoff.

kind.description: Free slug rather than an enum, because an enum would make an unclassifiable observation inexpressible and push it into silence. `unclassified` is the honest value when the class is not yet known — it is also what friction-loop defaults to.

observed.description: What was seen, stated as fact rather than as judgement.

consequence.description: Explicit null when the consequence is not yet known. Required-but-nullable rather than optional, so 'we did not work out the consequence' is written down instead of left out.

inferred.description: false when the instrument read this directly; true when a human or agent derived it from something the instrument read. An inferred observation that reads as measured is how a story becomes evidence.

evidenceRefs.description: Repository-relative paths or receipt identifiers a reader can open.

allOf.description: An inference must name what it was inferred FROM, or it is an opinion wearing an observation's schema.

coverage.description: The partition. Both keys are required even when one is empty, because `unobserved: {}` is a claim a reader can challenge while a missing key is not. Every dimension appears exactly once across the two maps — see the allOf below.

partitionOn.$comment: One entry per dimension. Each asserts exactly-once membership: present in observed and absent from unobserved, or the reverse. This is what makes a silently dropped dimension a schema violation rather than a quiet narrowing of scope.

decideFeedback.description: What LEARN sends back to DECIDE. The loop is only closed if the next OpportunityContract can be written from this object without re-reading the whole pack.

successCondition.description: Against the successCondition carried by the OpportunityContract at the head of this chain.

status.description: not-observable is a first-class outcome, not a failure to report. It is the correct answer whenever the dimensions the success condition depends on were never instrumented.

allOf.description: A verdict on the success condition must point at observations. Declaring success with nothing to point at is the vacuous pass at its most expensive.
'Not observable' must name WHICH unobserved dimensions made it so, and may not smuggle in supporting observations.

unknownsResolved.description: openUnknowns from the OpportunityContract that this pack answered.

unknownsStillOpen.description: openUnknowns the launch did not answer. Carried forward verbatim so the next DECIDE inherits them rather than re-deriving them.

newUnknowns.description: Questions the launch created that nobody had before.

instrumentationDebt.description: The unobserved set restated as work. Each entry is a candidate scope item for the next journey, derived from an unobserved dimension's wouldRequire.

observationWindow.description: The interval during which observation was even possible. Everything in coverage.observed must sit inside it; a finding dated outside the window came from somewhere this pack did not declare.

sources.description: May be empty — a launch with no observation sources at all is a legitimate and important thing to record, provided coverage.unobserved then accounts for all eight dimensions.

promotionAuthorized.description: A producer may write false. It may never write true. Promotion is derived from a signed approval by src/lib/repair-approval.mjs, never accepted as input.

evolutionEventRequired.description: Whether this pack's contents warrant a nodekit.evolution-event/v1 draft. This pack does NOT write one — the Evolution Ledger owns the decision record and its interpretation.status may only reach human-reviewed through a verified signed approval.

content.$comment: The propertyNames guard is redundant under additionalProperties:false and is kept as a named tripwire: if this object is ever loosened, self-approval fields still fail closed rather than silently becoming expressible. Written as propertyNames rather than `not`/`required` so it survives Ajv strict mode (strictRequired rejects a required property that is not declared in `properties`), and because it binds every property name rather than an enumerated list of shapes.
